name: J03 counterexample - a refused approval writes nothing
about: J03 counterexample - a REFUSED approval writes nothing, and leaves nothing
pending.
PURPOSE. The positive journey shows that an allowed tool runs. Alone that
cannot distinguish a client that asks properly from one whose prompt is
decorative and whose tool runs regardless. This is the other half.
Refusal uses each client's own binding: native binds r to reject in its
permission pane; the retained Prompt declares its escape key as reject, so
Escape selects Reject there rather than a key this scenario invented.
THE FILE MUST BE MISSING, not merely lacking a marker. missing is the
strict claim that nothing was written, so a refusal that wrote DIFFERENT
bytes cannot pass it. Asserted before the prompt and again after the
refusal.
THE REFUSED CALL MUST REACH A TERMINAL, and the two clients can prove that to
different depths. Say which is which rather than averaging them.
Native renders `tool shell error`, which IS a settled outcome, so the native
assertion names the terminal form. Asserting the bare tool name plus the
ABSENCE of `running` was weaker than it looked: a blank or still-updating view
satisfies an absence.
THE RETAINED VERB IS NOT A TERMINAL DISCRIMINATOR and is not used as one.
`index.tsx:2867` picks `Running` only while running, and otherwise `Ran`
whenever a command has parsed at all - and `:2870` keeps the spinner for
`status === "streaming"`. So a STREAMING call with a parsed command already
reads `Ran`. The retained step therefore establishes that the row and its
command are DISPLAYED, nothing more; settlement on that side is established
by correlating the durable tool call - session, call id and exact target -
against its error terminal after the run, and is reported as such.
A step SKIPPED for a client proves nothing about that client. An earlier
receipt reported this journey as passing on both clients when the positive
step was native-only; that was an overstatement and is not repeated.
The in-flight forms must ALSO be gone, which is the no-pending-waiter half.
That terminal is awaited BEFORE the no-effect claim is concluded, rather
than sampled while the tool might still be starting.
The filename and marker differ from the positive journey's so the two can
never satisfy each other, and each client is checked in its own recorded
effect_root.
WHAT CARRIES THE REFUSAL ON THE RETAINED SIDE, since a review named this as
a checkable suspect: NOT the token `Ran`. That is the identical token a
SUCCESSFUL shell draws in j03-approval, because the retained client marks a
denied tool with strikethrough styling rather than with different words —
checked in its own renderer, not assumed. `Ran` here proves only that a
settled shell row exists.
The refusal is carried by the two steps after it: `Running` must be ABSENT,
so the call settled rather than still going, and `j03-refused.txt` must
still be MISSING. That last one is an effect on disk, outside both clients
and unforgeable by either — no amount of fluent output creates a file. A
reader checking whether this scenario can tell a refusal from a success
should look there and not at `Ran`.
